Which of the following statements are true given that $T:{R}^{5}\to {R}^{5}$ is a linear transformation whose standard matrix is $T,$ and ${{v}_{1},{v}_{2},{v}_{3}}$ is a basis of $\text{Col}(T)?$

- $\text{rank}(T)=3$
- $T$ is invertible
- $\text{nullity}(T)>0$

activity_context.topic_title: The Invertible Matrix Theorem in Terms of Linear Transformations

feedback.problem:
Which of the following statements are true given that $T:{R}^{7}\to {R}^{7}$ is a linear transformation whose standard matrix is $T,$ and $T(x)=v$ has no solution for some vector $v?$ 

- $T$ is not invertible
- $\text{nullity}(T)=0$
- $\text{rank}(T)\ne 7$
feedback.worked_solution:
Since $T$ is a linear transformation from ${R}^{7}$ into ${R}^{7},$ the invertible matrix theorem states the following:

 $T$ is a bijection (an invertible transformation) $\,⟺\,{\,\begin{aligned} & \text{Im}(T)={R}^{7} \\  & \text{rank}(T)=7 \\  & \text{Ker}(T)={0} \\  & \text{nullity}(T)=0\end{aligned}$ 

With that in mind, let's examine each statement in turn.

- Statement I is true. Since $T(x)=v$ has no solution, we have that $v\notin \text{Im}(T),$ hence $\text{Im}(T)\ne {R}^{7}.$ According to the invertible matrix theorem, since $\text{Im}(T)\ne {R}^{7},$ the transformation $T$ and the matrix $T$ are not invertible.

- Statement II is false. Since $T$ is not invertible, the invertible matrix theorem implies that $\text{nullity}(T)\ne 0.$

- Statement III is true. Since $T$ is not invertible, the invertible matrix theorem implies that $\text{rank}(T)\ne 7.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only."
